key_insight: A two-level machine-learning framework can map the thermodynamic stability of complex hybrid perovskite alloys across composition space, revealing that Sn-based alloys have a much narrower stable region than Pb-based alloys.
engineering_relevance: The stability maps directly inform compositional engineering for perovskite solar cells, pointing to high-iodide compositions as the most promising route for robust materials.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to speed up structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes were computed for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, including disorder and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated by generating free-energy landscapes across compositions and phases, showing maximum stability at high I content and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on ML models trained on DFT data, accuracy may degrade outside the composition and phase space covered by training.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
